summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood (AE + SE) and Hyperion Cloud partnership team. Covered partner GTM alignment, high-level technical fit for private/VPC deployments, benchmarking plan for latency/cost, and security/compliance questions. Agreed on next steps: share partner deck, benchmark checklist, and schedule technical deep-dive.
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 16:00 PT / 19:00 ET
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Laura Mendoza (Hyperion Dir, Cloud Partnerships), Aaron Li (Hyperion CTO), Samir Patel (Hyperion Solutions Architect)
Recording: Yes
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you making time. I'm Ethan, one of the AEs on the Redwood partner team, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Priya Singh: Hi all, thanks, excited to chat. We'll keep this pretty informal — want to learn about Hyperion's partner motion and your infra needs.
[00:29] Laura Mendoza: Great, thanks Ethan and Priya. I'm Laura, I run Cloud Partnerships at Hyperion. Aaron and Samir are here from our infra and platform teams.
[00:39] Aaron Li: Hi — quick note, timing's tight for us, but we'll try to cover the main things.
[00:45] Samir Patel: Yep, thanks.
[00:48] Ethan Park: Awesome. Agenda for today: quick intros, high-level partnership goals, technical fit (private/VPC, dedicated pools), security/compliance, and then next steps. Does that work?
[01:00] Laura Mendoza: Yep, sounds good. Our main goal is to understand if Redwood is a good platform partner for us to resell and integrate into Hyperion's managed offering. We're looking at partner revenue, but also engineering lift.
[01:18] Priya Singh: Understood. Can you give a quick snapshot of typical Hyperion customers and what GPU hardware you're running in your clusters?
[01:27] Laura Mendoza: Mostly mid-market SaaS and a few enterprise accounts, want turnkey LLM endpoints for customers. We run a mix — Ampere and some NVidia H100s in our premium pools, plus A100 on older fleets.
[01:42] Aaron Li: We're exploring adding specialized GPU SKUs and partnerships so our customers can spin up fully-managed LLM inference. Latency and cost are the two big levers.
[01:52] Ethan Park: That aligns closely to partners we work with. A couple quick Qs on integration: do you expect a fully private deployment inside your VPC per customer, or would you prefer a hybrid where some hosted control plane talks to customer-owned inference?
[02:08] Samir Patel: We want both options. For smaller customers, an integrated hosted model is fine. For regulated customers, we need private VPC deployments and strict KMS control.
[02:19] Priya Singh: Ok good — Redwood supports hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem deployments. For private mode the control plane sits in your environment and you manage keys, or we can support customer-managed KMS/HSM.
[02:33] Aaron Li: How mature is the private control plane? Any large customers live on it?
[02:39] Priya Singh: Yes, a handful of enterprise customers are on private; it's production hardened. There are a few nuances — network setup, routing, and autoscaling policies need to be validated since we're balancing throughput and SLOs.
[02:52] Laura Mendoza: When you say 'production hardened' — curious about compliance: SOC 2, ISO, audit logs, and support for SSO/SAML for our teams.
[03:02] Ethan Park: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and we publish audit logs for requests. SSO is supported; SAML and OIDC are common. For private installs we can integrate with your identity provider.
[03:15] Samir Patel: Do you support token-level cost attribution — we need to show customers token spend and per-route cost?
[03:22] Priya Singh: Yes, that's in Redwood Console — token-level breakdowns, per-model and per-route dashboards. It helps with reseller billing and chargebacks.
[03:30] Aaron Li: Ok. On performance: we care about 95th percentile latency for generation under typical customer loads. Can you share kernel/compilation optimizations and what kind of latency we might expect on H100 vs A100?
[03:45] Priya Singh: Briefly: our runtime selects kernels based on model arch and sequence length distribution; we use attention optimizations and KV caching for chat-like workloads. On H100 we often see 20-30% better latency per token vs A100 for large context lengths, but depends on quantization and batch sizes.
[04:03] Laura Mendoza: Are the numbers public or is there a benchmark we can run?
[04:07] Ethan Park: We can share a benchmark checklist and a sample spreadsheet that maps latency/cost per model and hardware. Priya will send it.
[04:15] Priya Singh: I'll attach the checklist — includes payload sizes, seq lengths, concurrency settings, and how we measure warm vs cold KV cache.
[04:24] Samir Patel: Warm vs cold cache — how does your caching work? Is it prefix caching or a shared KV cache per model?
[04:31] Priya Singh: It's mostly prefix/KV caching with configurable TTL; we also do workload-aware batching. There is a small chance the transcript will have mis-reads — sorry — but basically it helps reduce per-token compute when the same prefixes repeat.
[04:44] Aaron Li: For our managed customers, we'd want to pin model versions and control rollouts — can we do canary deploys or A/B tests?
[04:52] Priya Singh: Yes, the Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to other model variants when capacity is constrained.
[05:00] Laura Mendoza: On pricing and revenue split — are partners resellers or referral partners? How flexible is the partner model?
[05:08] Ethan Park: We offer a flexible partner program: referral fee, revenue share for resellers, and white-label options for strategic partners. We tailor commitment levels for reserved capacity and enterprise features.
[05:19] Aaron Li: Would we be reselling Redwood Dedicated pools as part of Hyperion managed offering?
[05:24] Ethan Park: Yes, reselling Dedicated is common — you can offer reserved GPU pools under Hyperion branding while Redwood handles the runtime. We can negotiate pricing tiers based on commit.
[05:33] Laura Mendoza: Good. On technical integration — what's the typical onboarding timeline for a private deployment and what engineering resources are required from our side?
[05:42] Priya Singh: Typical timeline is 4-8 weeks for private/VPC depending on network setup, IAM, KMS integration, and test benchmarks. For dedicated it's often 2-4 weeks. Expect some infra time to set up VPC peering, firewall rules, and KMS access.
[05:58] Samir Patel: Do you require any specific CNI or is it cloud-agnostic? We run across AWS and in a few places on-prem.
[06:05] Priya Singh: It's cloud-agnostic — we support VPC setups on AWS, GCP, and Azure. For on-prem we have an installer package but there are a few environment-specific knobs.
[06:16] Aaron Li: Data residency — some customers require logs and metrics to never leave region, including embeddings and request metadata. Can Redwood enforce regional data residency?
[06:25] Ethan Park: Yes, we support region-restricted deployments and we can disable outbound telemetry for certain customers. For embeddings, we can opt to not persist or to store in customer-managed stores.
[06:36] Laura Mendoza: How do you handle encryption at rest and in transit? KMS integration specifics?
[06:41] Priya Singh: We support in-transit TLS, and at-rest encryption via KMS. For private installs we can use customer-managed KMS/HSM; we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSMs via standard APIs.
[06:53] Samir Patel: Nice. Switching gears — any gotchas around autoscaling or noisy neighbor on shared Dedicated pools?
[06:59] Priya Singh: For Dedicated we allow reserved pools with configurable autoscaling and burst capacity controls. Noisy neighbor risk is mitigated by strict isolation per pool, but it's important to size the VM/GPU instance types and batch settings correctly.
[07:13] Aaron Li: When customers run big batched jobs, do you support preemptible/spot instances to lower cost?
[07:19] Ethan Park: We can support spot/preemptible for non-SLA-critical workloads; for SLA-backed offerings we recommend reserved capacity.
[07:26] Laura Mendoza: For partner GTM — are there co-marketing resources and enablement?
[07:31] Ethan Park: Yes, partner kit includes co-branded deck, joint case studies, and sales training. We'll include that in the partner one-pager.
[07:38] Samir Patel: On API compatibility — how stable is the API and is there a migration path if we later self-host?
[07:45] Priya Singh: The API is stable and consistent across hosted, dedicated and private modes so you'll have minimal changes. We version models and APIs to avoid breaking changes.
[07:53] Aaron Li: Ok. A couple security details: do you provide per-request audit logs and an export for SIEMs?
[07:59] Priya Singh: Yes, audit logs and tracing hooks are exportable — we support export to S3 and common SIEMs. For private deployments we can push logs to your collectors.
[08:09] Laura Mendoza: Excellent. Commercial — what's your partner discounting and required commitment thresholds for reserved capacity?
[08:16] Ethan Park: That varies by partner tier. For resellers we do revenue-share models; for dedicated reserved capacity, commit levels start at a monthly baseline — we'll include sample pricing in the deck.
[08:26] Samir Patel: For benchmarking — what exactly do you need from us to run a meaningful perf test?
[08:31] Priya Singh: Ideally: representative workloads (prompts/payloads), typical concurrency, target latency percentiles, model family you'd like to run, and a few sequences for context lengths. Also whether embeddings are used and their dimensionality.
[08:45] Aaron Li: We'll share a sample workload — Samir will follow up.
[08:50] Laura Mendoza: On partner support — what's the SLA for incident response for private vs hosted?
[08:55] Ethan Park: Hosted has tiered SLAs; dedicated and private can get enterprise SLAs with faster response times and a named support contact. We'll surface SLA options in the partner materials.
[09:06] Priya Singh: One small note — sometimes product names get transcribed weirdly, so if you see 'Redwood Dedicate' in notes it's 'Redwood Dedicated'.
[09:15] Aaron Li: Ha, noted.
[09:18] Ethan Park: Any other technical blockers we should be aware of?
[09:22] Samir Patel: Network egress costs are a concern for some customers. If traffic flows between Hyperion and Redwood endpoints there could be charge implications.
[09:30] Priya Singh: That's fair — for private deployments that stays inside the VPC and reduces egress; for hosted modes we can discuss architecture to minimize cross-region traffic and cache results.
[09:42] Laura Mendoza: Another question — how granular is billing? We need per-customer, per-route attribution for resale.
[09:49] Ethan Park: Console has token-level cost breakdown and per-route billing exports; we can generate reports to match Hyperion's billing model.
[09:57] Aaron Li: Ok. For the technical deep-dive, we'd like to bring our infra lead and GPU ops person to validate kernel-level perf and scheduling. Can Priya run through kernel selection and quantization flow?
[10:10] Priya Singh: Absolutely — in the technical deep-dive we'll cover kernel selection heuristics, quantization profiles (INT8/4-bit), and how we tune batching for low latency.
[10:21] Samir Patel: Perfect. If possible include an example run with a 4k context LLM to see memory usage and latency curves.
[10:29] Priya Singh: We'll include that in the checklist.
[10:31] Laura Mendoza: Sounds like we're aligned. Let's talk timeline — we'd like to pilot with one or two customers in June. Is that feasible?
[10:39] Ethan Park: Yes, June pilot is feasible assuming we start infra validation in late April/May. We'll target a technical deep-dive in the week of Apr 27 and then infra onboarding in May.
[10:51] Laura Mendoza: Great. Anything else on compliance — contract redlines typically ask for data processing agreement specifics and subprocessor lists. Do you have a standard DPA?
[10:59] Ethan Park: We have a standard DPA and a subprocessor list; I'll include them in the partner packet. For private deployments many customers prefer to keep Redwood out of the data plane which helps reduce DPA friction.
[11:12] Aaron Li: Quick note — our legal team also asks about export controls for models; some customers can't run certain model weights. Any guardrails?
[11:20] Priya Singh: We can enforce model catalogs per customer and restrict models that are allowed. Our catalog is curated and we can block or white-list models per tenant.
[11:29] Samir Patel: Cool.
[11:31] Ethan Park: Ok, let's recap real quick. Action items: Ethan sends partner deck and DPA; Priya sends benchmark checklist and sample perf spreadsheet; Samir to send representative workload; schedule technical deep-dive week of Apr 27. Anything to add?
[11:48] Laura Mendoza: That covers it. We'll expect the materials and will confirm the deep-dive attendees.
[11:55] Aaron Li: Thanks everyone.
[12:00] Ethan Park: Thanks team — we'll follow up via email with links. Talk soon.
references: DPA and subprocessor list (to be sent)
